Importing data

First step in data analysis

How do you get your data in workspace?

  • data in R packages

  • data from other sources

    • different formats (e.g. csv, sav, txt, excel)

    • from internet

Data from R packages

Many R packages contain data:

  • type data(), place the cursor between the parentheses, and hit TAB

    • the pop-up menu shows all datasets in the loaded packages

    • get more info with help(<data>, package = <package>)

Interactively importing data

  • text files (comma-, tab-, space-delimited)

  • data files from other statistical programs (SPSS, SAS, Stata)

  • excel files (.xls, .xlsx)

Joining data sets

Functions for joining data

Data frames joined by "x1"

Houseprices and gdp

Download the csv data sets and import in workspace

  • houseprices

  • gdp

Example code for the houseprices data:

library(readr)
hp <- read_csv("houseprices.csv", 
               n_max = 27,
               skip = 1,
               col_names = c("country", "houseprice"),
               show_col_types = F)

Join housesprices and gdp

Display a summary of both data sets

Depending on the result, join the data on country with

  • full_join()
  • left_join() or right_join()
  • inner_join()

given that you do not want missing values in the new data set.

Tydying data

Concept of tidy data

Tidyverse is developed for tidy data:

  • variables measuring the same thing form a single variable


  • untidy versus tidy data

Pivoting

The function to tidy data (in its simplest form) is:

pivot_longer(data, cols, names_to, names_prefix, values_to)
  • data the untidy data set
  • cols, columns to pivot
  • names_to name of the new variable
  • names_prefix separate the name and number of the columns to pivot
  • values_to name of the variable with the values

Example

(df <- data.frame(id = 1:3, obs1 = c(4, 9,5), obs2 = c(2, 6, 4)))
  id obs1 obs2
1  1    4    2
2  2    9    6
3  3    5    4

pivot_longer(df, cols = -id, 
             names_to = "obs", 
             names_prefix ="obs", 
             values_to = "score")
# A tibble: 6 × 3
     id obs   score
  <int> <chr> <dbl>
1     1 1         4
2     1 2         2
3     2 1         9
4     2 2         6
5     3 1         5
6     3 2         4
